messages:
sienna: FYI CS escalated — acmehealth (Dedicated us-west-2) saw a sudden throughput drop ~08:12 UTC, lots of 429s and tail latency. Dashboard: low GPU util, high queue depth.
carol: Confirming, their app logs show spike in 429s. No config changes on their side.
eli: What workload shape? tiny prompts or long generations?
carol: Mix: ~600 rps of small prompts (10-30 tokens) + occasional long requests. They suspect noisy neighbor.
maya: Infra snapshot: continuous-batcher queue depth surged; scheduler emitted many micro-batches (1-3 reqs) -> low GPU efficiency. Pasting logs.
ops-bot: [alert] pod/continuous-batcher-5 restarted 08:14:12 UTC (queue-slice preemption).
devon: Need batcher metrics 08:10-08:20: max_batch_tokens, batch_window_ms, tokens_per_batch.
maya: Metrics @08:10:
```
time=08:10
queue_depth=1200
avg_req_tokens=18
max_batch_tokens=2048
observed_batch_tokens=64,128,256 (most frequent)
gpu_util=28%
emitted_batches_per_min=720
```
eli: Classic token-slicing fragmentation: tiny requests prevent filling GPU-friendly token batches; scheduler flushes early hitting window or limits -> many kernel launches.
sienna: Carol, can CS reproduce? we need a short load script with tenant header.
carol: Repro script (simulates 600rps small prompts):
```
while true; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"X-Tenant: acmehealth\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\",\"max_tokens\":12}'; done
```
carol: App traces: many responses ~120ms but queue latency high; GPU busy-time per-token low.
eli: Two mitigations to try quickly:
1) Increase max_batch_tokens or extend batch_window_ms so scheduler can accumulate more small requests into larger token-packed batches.
2) Apply per-tenant smoothing (token-leaky-bucket admission) to damp bursts until scheduler is improved.
maya: Suggest experiment: override for tenant: {\"max_batch_tokens\":16384, \"batch_window_ms\":40} (default window 15ms). Also monitor preemption logs.
devon: Canary plan: apply override to pool us-west-2 for acmehealth, monitor 20m, auto-rollback on regressions.
oncall-bot: Rollout scheduled: scheduler-config update for cluster us-west-2 (override for acmehealth) by maya in 2m. Auto-rollback if 429 rate increases or gpu_util < 20%.
sienna: If preemption continues we may pin tenant to dedicated batcher or create exclusion pool.
maya: Override applied 08:22 UTC. Immediate metrics after change:
```
08:23 snapshot
queue_depth=320
observed_batch_tokens=2048,8192,12100
emitted_batches_per_min=160
gpu_util=82%
response_p95=85ms (prev 420ms)
429_rate=0.2% (prev 7%)
```
rachel: CS confirms customer sees latency restored and almost no errors. No traffic change on their end.
carol: Thanks. Do we keep override or make global change?
eli: Keep override for 48h to collect signals. Long-term: scheduler improvements needed — token-aware packing, adaptive windows, avoid preemption that fragments many small-token workloads.
maya: Filed INFRA-2345: \"scheduler: preferential token packing + adaptive windowing to avoid micro-batches under small-token regimes\" with repro and metrics from thread.
devon: Ops action items:
- keep override 48h
- add tokens_emitted_per_batch histogram metric
- author runbook for tenant-induced fragmentation (pin tenant, override, apply admission control)
sienna: Thanks all. Carol/CS keep me posted; will close escalation after 48h stable. :white_check_mark:
carol: Will update if anything recurs, uploading graphs to ticket.
oncall-bot: Reminder: rollback window ends 09:10 UTC if no anomalies detected.
